A mortgaged sale is one financed by a bank loan with a mortgage on the home; its share shows the proportion of homes bought on credit.
m.TÜİK-TCMB Tüketici Eğilim Anketi'nde han: In the TURKSTAT-CBRT Consumer Tendency Survey, households are asked how likely they are to spend money on repairing their home over the next 12 months; the CBRT series definition mentions heating systems, painting and kitchen or bathroom repairs. Answers are converted into an index from 0 to 200: 100 means those who will spend and those who will not are balanced; below 100 means those who will not spend outweigh the others. 42.5 is a low level, but it has risen from 35.1 a year earlier.

s: E-Commerce Growth Opportunities: Demand, User Behaviour and Channel Model
Sanitaryware (SSG) demand · 3-year change; bathroom furniture (BM) -21.6%
Monthly inner-mechanism and spare-part searches · extended keyword universe; no separate spare-parts category on the site
Share of bathroom furniture searches naming a retailer · naming VitrA 1.5%

Search demand for bathroom products is declining and the two main groups diverge: monthly searches for sanitaryware such as WCs and washbasins (SSG) fell modestly over three years (-3.2%), while bathroom furniture (BM) fell 21.6%. The improvement in consumer confidence and home repair intent has not yet reached search demand; these indicators can be monitored for the timing of a recovery

VitrA's brand searches hold up while category searches contract; in taps and mixers brand demand goes to competitors: searches combining "vitra" with a category phrase are up 11.4% since 2023, at 144K a month. VitrA accounts for 28.4% of brand + category searches across 26 manufacturer brands and is the most searched brand in sanitaryware, cisterns, bathroom furniture and tiles; in tap brand searches, however, E.C.A. (40.6%) and Artema (25.9%) are ahead and VitrA's share is 10.1%

Interest in spare parts is high but the site has no separate spare-parts category or part finder: inner mechanisms, float valves, hinges, cartridges and gaskets are searched on Google about 133K times a month. Inner mechanisms are sold on the site, but there is no separate spare-parts category; the old spare-parts page redirects to a category containing a single product

VitrA's services exist but are not offered as one package: the site has 11 separate installation services, on-site survey and furniture with free installation, but these are not combined into a single "product + installation + survey" offer. Installation or survey options do not appear on pages of products such as shower enclosures that cannot be chosen without measuring

There is demand in products close to the brand that VitrA sells only in part or not at all today: sinks (kitchen sinks; 225K searches a month; VitrA offers ceramic sinks only, no granite or steel sinks), and products for elderly, accessible and children's bathrooms; demand for purifier taps is smaller (3.8K a month). In towel radiators and LED mirrors the product range is narrow relative to demand

VitrA products on marketplaces are sold largely through third-party sellers: on Hepsiburada, the "add to basket" button (buybox) for VitrA products is won by third-party sellers 69% of the time, by Hepsiburada 13% and by the VitrA store 19%. VitrA products on marketplaces are typically priced at 1.5x-6x the best sellers in the same category: about 1.5x in WC sets, 2x in WCs and up to 6x in bathroom cabinets. In bathroom furniture VitrA may stand out through set, installation and warranty advantages rather than price

Complaints mainly concern the after-purchase process: 76.9% of the 581 readable VitrA complaints (of 600) on Şikayetvar in the last 24 months mention at least one of service, spare parts, installation or reaching customer service. VitrA's Şikayetvar brand score is 18 out of 100. The share of spare-part complaints rose from 8.1% in Oct 2024 - Mar 2025 to 17.8% in Apr - Sep 2026

The same VitrA product is often sold cheaper on marketplaces than on vitra.com.tr: for 19 of the 29 VitrA products reviewed, the lowest price is not on vitra.com.tr but at a seller on Hepsiburada, Trendyol or Koçtaş. For these 19 products the lowest marketplace price is typically 24.7% lower than the vitra.com.tr list price (median; 29.8% for taps). For example, a product priced at ₺1,000 on the site can be found for about ₺750 on a marketplace; with the site's basket discount the gap falls to 15.4%. On Google Shopping, the VitrA site appears in 9 of the 24 products whose sellers are listed, and in these products its price is typically 37% above the lowest seller price. In 15 of 27 category searches the VitrA site does not appear in Google Shopping results at all

Most products on vitra.com.tr category pages do not appear in stock: 71.1% of the 2,258 product options (colour and size variants) on the 55 sub-category pages reviewed (excluding the main basin unit, tall cabinet, wall-hung WC and tile lists) fall outside the "in stock" filter, and 13 sub-categories have no product in stock at all. 89.9% of first-page products carry an "N% off in basket" label, so the price shown on the card is not the price paid. The same model code sells on marketplaces typically 14.4% below the vitra.com.tr list price, close to the site's basket price

Purchase steps on vitra.com.tr take the user through more screens than needed: a user who wants to buy without an account passes two intermediate screens before the address step (a sign-in panel and a separate e-mail screen) after "Confirm cart". In site search, instant results while typing mostly return relevant products, but the results page after Enter is empty or off-target for 9 of the 38 test terms (and for 3 terms the instant results are empty or off-target instead); cartridge, seal, spare part, warranty and service searches return no relevant product or support page on either path. Installation services and recommendation areas in the cart sit at the bottom of the page. One-step guest purchase in the cart and aligning the two search paths so each search returns the more accurate result are conversion opportunities under the site's own control

In the official VitrA store on Trendyol, unit sales grew while the average price fell: units sold rose 4.3 times over the last four quarters while the average selling price fell from ₺3,539 to ₺1,688; growth comes mainly from low-priced products such as angle valves and accessories. In bathroom furniture, taps and showers, which stand out in the store's revenue, the official store is absent from Trendyol's September 2026 best-seller lists; 73% of VitrA products in these lists are sold through other sellers. 27.6% of returns are due to the size not fitting and 19.2% to ordering the wrong product

Google's AI features are reducing clicks to blog articles: the share of AI features in site impressions rose from 4.3% in the last two weeks of May to 6.5% in September, reaching 12.4% on blog pages (18 May - 29 Sep 2026). In June - September, blog clicks changed -25.0% against 2025 while impressions changed +4.7%; in the 12 articles where 20% or more of impressions are in AI features, clicks changed -50.6% while the average position held. For these articles the goal can be defined as being cited in the AI answer as well as the click

vitra.com.tr's e-commerce revenue rose 87.4% in January - September 2026 against the same months of 2025, and organic search's share of revenue rose from 31.3% to 46.0%: the number of purchases rose 54.2% to 2,473 and the average order value increased from ₺9.5K to ₺11.6K. Traffic from AI assistants produced ₺263K of revenue in the same period. 49.7% of revenue appears in sessions starting directly on the order confirmation page, and the page that started the purchase is lost in these sessions; WhatsApp and phone requests are not tracked as separate events in GA4, and promotion clicks are not linked to purchases. Therefore the effect of campaigns, content and the product + service flow on sales cannot be fully measured today.

Marketplaces take the top positions in product and category searches on Google: Trendyol is in the top 10 results for 134 of the 159 product and category searches in VitrA's range. VitrA is in the top 3 for sanitaryware such as WCs and washbasins and for bath and basin taps; it does not appear in the top 20 for complementary taps such as bidet taps and robot shower sets, and is also outside the top 10 for products bought together with the bathroom such as water purifiers and water heaters. None of the 14 most-viewed repair, installation and product choice topics on YouTube shows a VitrA channel video

In marketplace reviews the negative share for VitrA is slightly above competitors, with a clear gap in bathroom cabinets: on Trendyol and Hepsiburada the share of 1-2 star reviews is 12.1% for VitrA products, 8.0% for Artema and 10.1% for competitor brands. For VitrA and Artema bathroom cabinets the share of low-rated reviews is 17.9% (competitors 7.5%), and 58.0% of these reviews mention the product arriving broken, damaged or defective. 31.9% of questions on VitrA products are compatibility and place-of-use questions such as "will this product fit my WC or plumbing"

The biggest opportunity for visibility in AI-assisted search (Google AI Overview, ChatGPT and similar) lies in problem-solving content: 35.3% of clicks to vitra.com.tr guide articles come from installation, repair and cleaning topics, while the 23 frequently asked questions (FAQ) pages and about 530 questions in the support section are scattered: 4 pages still carry a template title ("Accelerator Title") and have no Q&A markup, and 4 product groups have duplicate FAQ pages. VitrA is cited as a source in 24 of the 54 searches in VitrA's range where Google's AI summaries (AI Overview) were reviewed; 506 of the 2,140 keywords tracked in SEOmonitor show an AI Overview, and VitrA is cited in 38% of them. In 111 questions without a brand name asked to ChatGPT, Gemini and AI Overview, VitrA is the manufacturer brand named most often, in 52-74% of answers; however for questions close to purchase such as where to buy, delivery and returns, the sources cited are mostly Koçtaş, Trendyol and Bauhaus. Making the VitrA records on Wikidata and Wikipedia consistent can help the brand be introduced correctly in AI answers

Economic Environment: Spending, Confidence and Housing Market

The general economic conditions that affect demand for bathroom products are tracked with four indicator groups covering how much people spend by card, their confidence in the economy and intention to have their homes repaired, house sales and banks' lending conditions. Because bathroom renovation is a spending that can be postponed, these indicators help explain the background to the contraction in category searches (Section 03). The data come from the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye's data system (CBRT EVDS).

Spending grows in nominal terms and rises only modestly in real terms (card payment index +8.6%); total house sales fell 6.8% while mortgaged sales rose 27.6%; confidence and repair intent are climbing, and credit conditions are easing but credit demand has not yet revived.
This combination points to accumulated, postponed renovation demand.
For the e-commerce channel, price, instalment and delivery clarity can be treated as priorities so that it becomes the first point of contact when demand returns.
Estimate of annual bathroom renovations and new-home bathrooms
Scenarios for the annual number of bathrooms from households, new homes and an assumed renovation cycle, and public indicators for VitrA's share; the rates are assumptions, not measurements.
No source directly measures annual bathroom renovations in Turkey; the estimate is built from households, new homes and the renovation cycle.

Assuming 26.6 million households, an average of 0.58 million completed dwellings a year and 1.2 bathrooms per home, the annual bathroom count is about 2.1 million at a 4.5% renovation rate and 1.7-2.6 million between 3% and 6%.

Development areas derived from VitrA reviews, question clusters and competitors' common pain points; ▲ issues recommended to address, ✓ areas offering a chance to stand out.

Bathroom cabinet delivery: the negative share is 17.9% in VitrA and Artema bathroom cabinet reviews and 7.5% for competitors; 58.0% of negative reviews mention broken or damaged products and 52.0% the return and exchange process. Reinforcing protective packaging for sets containing a washbasin and mirror and shortening the exchange process for damaged deliveries may be considered.

Compatibility information: 31.9% of VitrA questions are about compatibility and place of use, 18.3% about box contents and 18.9% about size. Adding a compatible model list, a dimension drawing and a set contents table to product pages may reduce the question load and shorten the decision stage.

Official store answers: on Hepsiburada, 29.5% of questions on VitrA products and 19.0% on Artema products were answered by the official store; the rest are answered by other sellers of the same product. Extending the official store's question follow-up to all VitrA and Artema listings may ensure product information comes from a single source.

Installation support: installation is among the most frequent pain points at competitors (55.0% of negative reviews at Durul); at VitrA installation appears in 14.7% of negative reviews (competitors 16.8%). Making installation videos and the setup guide visible on the product page can reduce questions on this topic.

After-sales contact: returns, exchanges and seller contact appear in 34.9% of VitrA's negative reviews (25.4% at competitors, highest at Turkuaz with 42.3%). Stating return and exchange steps clearly on official store product pages and a fast exchange process for damaged deliveries can reduce this share.

Reducing guest purchase to a single step in the cart

Aligning the two site search paths and routing part and support searches

Making installation services and complementary products visible in the cart
The installation and "VitrA picks for you" carousels can be made smaller and moved directly below the cart list; the installation service matching the product can be suggested on the product row.
Managing out-of-stock products in lists and search
Moving out-of-stock cards to the end, an estimated restock date or a close alternative can help keep the user on the site.
A clear price and warranty message on the product page
Showing the in-cart discount on the product page and the warranty period can reduce uncertainty at the point of decision.

Prioritisation considers ease of implementation and closeness to purchase together: checkout flow and site search come into play when the user is closest to buying and are under the site's own control. The order of actions can be updated with the VitrA team's priorities.
